problem.text: Relaxations of the KNRS conjecture and their consequences for subdivisions.

claims.text: Theorem 1.2 and 1.3: for every graph F, t(F, W^{oq}) >= rho^{q e(F)} for every rho-locally dense graphon W when q >= binom(n,2)/e(F), with W^{oq} the Hadamard power. Proposition 1.4: regular-KNRS implies that the 1-subdivision is Sidorenko; KNRS and Sidorenko-good each imply regular-KNRS. Theorems 1.5 and 1.6: theta-subdivision results. Corollary 1.7: every graph becomes KNRS after adding a disjoint multigraph.

assumptions.text: Graphon forms of KNRS and regular-KNRS; Sidorenko-good means the inequality on doubly nonnegative kernels; the regular reduction (Im, Li and Liu, Lemma 2.2).

methods.text: Hölder uniformization over vertex relabellings; positive semidefiniteness of operator powers and of Hadamard products.

evidence.text: Complete proofs, including Appendix A for Proposition 1.4.

limitations.text: The L^q statement is a relaxation, not the KNRS conjecture; regular-KNRS and Sidorenko-goodness are known only for restricted families.

relevance.text: No result of this paper decides the statement or a declared neighbour. For the 1-subdivision neighbour it sharpens the known sufficient condition: the 1-subdivision of G is Sidorenko when G is regular-KNRS, in particular when G is KNRS or Sidorenko-good. For the neighbour on S(H0), this gives: S(H0) is Sidorenko if the reported counterexample H0 is regular-KNRS, in particular if H0 satisfies Sidorenko's inequality on every doubly nonnegative kernel; the paper does not treat H0.
